title: Much (of), many (of), a lot of, lots (of)
summary: Как выбирать между **much/many**, **a lot of / lots of** и **much of / many of**: стиль, утверждение и отрицание, согласование и устойчивые выражения.
ru:
## much / many и a lot of: где какое
**Much** (с неисчисляемыми) и **many** (со счётными) в современном английском чаще всего встречаются в **отрицаниях и вопросах**: *We don't have much time. Did many people come?* В **утверждениях** нейтральная речь предпочитает **a lot of / lots of / plenty of**.
> I have **a lot of** work today. — У меня сегодня много работы.
> ~~I have much work today.~~ — звучит неестественно или книжно.

Но **many** в утверждении совершенно нормально, особенно в формальном стиле и с подлежащим: *Many people believe that…* А **much** в утверждении встречается в официальном письме и в устойчивых моделях: *Much has been written about this. There is much to be said for the plan.*

## Где much и many обязательны
После **so, too, as, how, very** (и **not**) используют именно **much / many**, а не **a lot of**:
> There were **too many** cars. — Машин было слишком много.
> **How much** does it cost? — Сколько это стоит?
> I don't have **as much** time as you. — У меня не так много времени, как у тебя.
> Thanks **very much**. — Большое спасибо.
- Помните различие: *much too expensive* (слишком дорого — усиливаем **too**) и *too much money* (слишком много денег).

## much of / many of
Если мы говорим о **части конкретного целого**, добавляется **of** и определитель (**the, this, her, my, these**) либо местоимение. Без определителя **of** не нужен.
> **Much of the** town was damaged. — Значительная часть города пострадала.
> **Many of her** colleagues disagreed. — Многие из её коллег были не согласны.
> I haven't read **many of them**. — Я прочитал не многие из них.
- ~~Many of people~~ → **Many** people / **Many of the** people
- Название места или времени: **Much of Asia**, **much of the time**, **much of the day** — без артикля перед именем собственным.

Классическое выражение: **not much of a + существительное** = «не особо...». *It wasn't much of a party. I'm not much of a cook.*

## Согласование глагола
Глагол согласуется с существительным **после of**, а не с самим «a lot».
> **A lot of money was** wasted. (неисчисляемое → ед. число)
> **A lot of people were** angry. (счётное → мн. число)
> **Much of the report is** out of date.
> **Many of the findings have** been questioned.

## Усиление и книжные выражения
Вместо **a lot of** в более формальной речи используют **a great deal of** (неисчисляемые) и **a large number of / a great many / a good many** (счётные). Литературно: **many a** + ед. число: *Many a student has struggled with this rule.* — Не один студент мучился с этим правилом.

## a lot без существительного
**A lot** и **lots** могут быть наречием или местоимением. В отрицании вместо них — **much**: *She travels a lot, but she doesn't earn much. 'Did you learn anything?' 'Yes, a lot.'*
en:
## much / many vs a lot of
**Much** (uncountable) and **many** (countable) are mostly used in **negatives and questions**: *We don't have much time. Did many people come?* In **positive statements**, neutral English prefers **a lot of / lots of / plenty of**.
> I have **a lot of** work today.
> ~~I have much work today.~~ (unnatural or very formal)

**Many** is fine in a positive sentence, especially in formal style and as part of a subject: *Many people believe that...* **Much** appears in formal writing and fixed patterns: *Much has been written about this. There is much to be said for the plan.*

## Where much and many are required
After **so, too, as, how, very** (and **not**) we use **much / many**, not **a lot of**:
> There were **too many** cars.
> **How much** does it cost?
> I don't have **as much** time as you.
> Thanks **very much**.
- Note the difference: *much too expensive* (**too** is strengthened) and *too much money*.

## much of / many of
To talk about **part of a specific whole**, add **of** plus a determiner (**the, this, her, my, these**) or a pronoun. Without a determiner, no **of**.
> **Much of the** town was damaged.
> **Many of her** colleagues disagreed.
> I haven't read **many of them**.
- ~~Many of people~~ → **Many** people / **Many of the** people
- With place names and time: **much of Asia**, **much of the time**, **much of the day**.

A fixed phrase: **not much of a + noun** = 'not a very good...'. *It wasn't much of a party. I'm not much of a cook.*

## Verb agreement
The verb agrees with the noun after **of**, not with 'a lot'.
> **A lot of money was** wasted.
> **A lot of people were** angry.
> **Much of the report is** out of date.
> **Many of the findings have** been questioned.

## More formal options
In formal English, **a great deal of** (uncountable) and **a large number of / a great many / a good many** (countable) replace **a lot of**. Literary: **many a** + singular: *Many a student has struggled with this rule.*

## a lot without a noun
**A lot** and **lots** can be an adverb or a pronoun. In negatives use **much**: *She travels a lot, but she doesn't earn much. 'Did you learn anything?' 'Yes, a lot.'*
structure:
## Форма → когда → пример
| Форма | Когда | Пример |
|---|---|---|
| **much** + неисчисл. | отрицание, вопрос, после so/too/as/how/very | We don't have **much** time. |
| **many** + счётное | отрицание, вопрос; формально и в утверждении | **Many** experts disagree. |
| **a lot of / lots of** | нейтральное утверждение | She has **a lot of** ideas. |
| **a great deal of** | формально, неисчисл. | **A great deal of** effort went into it. |
| **a great many / a large number of** | формально, счётное | **A great many** people attended. |
| **much of / many of** + определитель | часть целого | **Much of the** day was wasted. |
| **not much of a** + сущ. | оценка: «так себе» | He's **not much of a** singer. |

## Формулы
> **much / many of** + the / this / my / them + глагол по существительному
> **a lot of** + сущ. → глагол по существительному
> **many a** + ед. число (литературное)

## Наречие vs местоимение
| Утверждение | Отрицание / вопрос |
|---|---|
| She reads **a lot**. | She doesn't read **much**. |
| It costs **a lot**. | Does it cost **much**? |

exercises.title: much, many, much of, many of
exercises.example: We didn't have ___ time. → We didn't have **much** time.

items.text: We didn't spend {{much}} time on the introduction.
{{Many of}} the problems were caused by poor planning.
{{Much of}} the town was destroyed in the flood.
I haven't read {{many of}} his novels.
She spends {{much of}} her free time volunteering.

exercises.title: a lot или much?
exercises.instruction: Вставьте **a lot** (или **lots**) либо **much**. Это наречие или местоимение без существительного.
exercises.example: She travels ___, but she doesn't earn ___. → She travels **a lot**, but she doesn't earn **much**.

items.text: She travels {{a lot|lots}} for work, but she doesn't earn {{much}}.
Thank you very {{much}} for your help.
He was {{much}} too tired to drive.
Is the new office better? — Yes, it's {{much|a lot|lots}} better.

items.q: ___ of the evidence was destroyed in the fire.
items.why: Evidence неисчисляемое: **much of**; **many** требует множественного числа.

items.q: Not ___ people turned up to the meeting.
We've got ___ of work to finish before Friday.
items.why: **A lot of work** — нейтральная утвердительная форма; **much of work** без определителя невозможно.

items.q: I don't have ___ of a choice.
items.why: Устойчивое **not much of a + существительное** = «выбора почти нет».

items.q: ___ people believe that the economy will recover soon.
items.why: People — счётное, **Many** — нормально в утверждении как часть подлежащего.

items.q: There ___ a lot of traffic on the road yesterday.
She's ___ better than she was last week.
items.why: Перед сравнительной степенью — **much** (или **a lot**), но не **a lot of**.

exercises.title: Естественно или нет?
exercises.instruction: Выберите правильный или наиболее естественный вариант.

items.q: Какой вариант наиболее естественен в разговоре?
options: I have much work to do today.
I have a lot of work to do today.
I have many works to do today.
items.why: В нейтральном утверждении неисчисляемое **work** → **a lot of**; **works** здесь неверно.

options: Much of people I interviewed were unhappy.
Many of the people I interviewed were unhappy.
Many of people I interviewed were unhappy.
items.why: После **many of** нужен определитель (**the**); people — счётное, поэтому **many**.

items.q: A lot of students ___ taking the exam this year.
Much of the information ___ out of date.
Many a student ___ struggled with this rule.
There were too ___ people in the lift.
items.why: После **too** используется **much/many**, а people — счётное: **too many**.

exercises.title: Перепишите, используя указанную форму
exercises.instruction: Перепишите предложение, используя то, что в скобках.

items.prompt: (Use much of + passive) We spent a large part of the day in meetings.
answers: Much of the day was spent in meetings.

items.prompt: (Use many of) A large number of the guests were relatives.
answers: Many of the guests were relatives.

items.prompt: (Use not many of) Only a few of the shops were open.
answers: Not many of the shops were open.

items.prompt: (Use a great deal of) She has a lot of influence in the party.
answers: She has a great deal of influence in the party.

items.prompt: (Use a great many) Many people signed the petition.
answers: A great many people signed the petition.

items.prompt: (Use too much) The soup contains more salt than it should.
answers: The soup contains too much salt.
There is too much salt in the soup.
There's too much salt in the soup.

exercises.title: Формальный и разговорный стиль
exercises.instruction: Перепишите предложение, используя то, что в скобках.

items.prompt: (Use Much has) People have written a lot about this topic.
answers: Much has been written about this topic.

items.prompt: (Use Many) A lot of people think the policy is unfair.
answers: Many people think the policy is unfair.

items.prompt: (Use much) We don't have a lot of time.
answers: We do not have much time.
We have not got much time.

items.prompt: (Use many of) A lot of my colleagues don't agree.
answers: Many of my colleagues don't agree.
Many of my colleagues do not agree.

items.prompt: (Use much of) A big part of the film was shot in Iceland.
answers: Much of the film was shot in Iceland.

items.prompt: (Use How much) What is the price of a single ticket?
answers: How much is a single ticket?
How much does a single ticket cost?

exercises.title: Напишите о себе
exercises.instruction: Ответьте полными предложениями, используя **much (of)**, **many (of)** или **a lot of**.

items.prompt: How much free time do you have during the week?
items.sample: I don't have much free time during the week, because I work late.

items.prompt: Talk about your city. What are there a lot of there?
items.sample: There are a lot of cafes and parks in my city, but not many museums.

items.prompt: How do you usually spend your weekends? Use much of.
items.sample: I spend much of the weekend with my family.

items.prompt: Describe your friends. Use many of.
items.sample: Many of my friends are teachers, and a few are engineers.

items.prompt: What are you not much of a fan of? Use not much of a.
items.sample: I'm not much of a fan of fast food.

items.prompt: Write about something you have too much or too many of.
items.sample: I have too many apps on my phone, and I use too much time on them.
